Question 1 [3 marks]: How does Green invite the reader to consider aspects of the human sense of smell?
STIMULUS / TEXTS PROVIDED:
Text 1 — Nonfiction extract
Due to copyright restrictions, this material cannot be displayed until permission has been obtained.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 3):
3 marks: Explains effectively how Green invites the reader to consider aspects of the human sense of smell using appropriate supporting evidence
2 marks: Explains how Green invites the reader to consider aspects of the human sense of smell using some supporting evidence
1 marks: Provides some relevant information about the text

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Green invites the reader to consider how smell is the one human sense that cannot yet be replicated or reproduced. He shares a personal anecdote of his virtual reality experience on a roller coaster, describing how the ride ‘felt breath-stealingly real’ but the inaccurate imitation scent ‘wrenched’ him from his ‘state of joyfully suspended disbelief’. He expands on this point by challenging the reader to consider how humans are unable to accurately imagine and write about smell and ‘based on those stories’ even AI would get it ‘spectacularly wrong’.
